_banner: GENERATED FILE - do not edit by hand.
configs/data_video1_rules_dev.json, which is the configuration every
threshold was measured against. The organizers' harness calls
solution.detect_events(video_path) with no config argument, so this file
is what actually runs in the submission.

_note: Thresholds measured by scripts/calibrate_motion_thresholds.py over
63924 motion windows: a stationary vehicle has net <= 20px, a moving
one >= 31px, so net_max 25px sits between the two populations.
tolerance_gap 1.5s merges jitter-fragmented stops into one segment
(bus #529: raw max 15.3s contiguous, true 33.4s).
The 7 events this produces are all in the east leg / lower junction,
downstream of the calibrated stop line, where no signal is readable
from this camera. They are queue-like but are left reported rather than
suppressed, because suppressing them would mean inventing a signal
state. See camera.md, Known ambiguity item 2.
Lanes 0-3 are the directional lanes rebuilt from measurement:
0/1 are the westbound carriageway, 2/3 the eastbound one. Opposing
share fell from 82.8/70.6/42.7/8.9 percent to 0.7/0.5/1.8/3.5 over
the same 10200 frames, and the rule produces 0 events on both sample
videos while still firing on synthetic violations in all four lanes
(scripts/validate_wrong_way_detection.py).
The residual 3.5 percent in lane 3 is deceleration into a queue, not
wrong-way driving: every candidate was inspected individually.
Fires on the vehicle's FRONT crossing the stop line while the head
that governs the line is red. Yellow is deliberately not treated as
red, and an unreadable head leaves the rule silent rather than
assuming a state.
The governing head is matched by declared approach direction, not by
image position: a signal head is mounted high, so its ROI projects
above the road point it governs. See SceneContext.signal_for_line.
Stopped PAST the line on red, without entering the junction. The end
condition is the official one: the signal turning green clears the
event, which is why the colour is re-read every frame rather than
latched at the start.
Group-level: standstill or crawling across every lane of one travel
direction, so a single stopped car can never raise it. A standing
queue at a red light is excluded, since that is the road working as
designed rather than congestion.
A pedestrian on the carriageway and outside every calibrated
crossing. Standing on the road is not jaywalking, because the official
definition is about entering the carriageway. The start is taken from
the moment the pedestrian's bottom centre left non-road, so it is not
anchored to whichever frame first noticed.
Requires an interaction: a pedestrian inside (or stepping onto) a
crossing and a vehicle passing through that same crossing while still
moving. A vehicle that halts for the pedestrian is compliant and is
excluded, and proximity on its own is never sufficient.
Requires the vehicle to change SIDES of the marking, which separates
a real crossing from a vehicle tracking along a line, and requires the
crossing to be over the drawn segment rather than past its end. The
calibrated markings here are the road edges and the median kerb, so
crossing one of them is a genuine violation.
Judged from the lane's declared allowed_moves, never from the fact
that a vehicle turned. A vehicle that changes lane while still
following its lane direction is a lane change and is excluded, and a
turn through the junction (where no lane applies) is not judged at
all because there is no lane to be wrong about.
The manoeuvre is recovered from trajectory history as a sustained
heading reversal that returns towards its origin, which is what
separates a U-turn from driving through the junction.
Prohibition is claimed only from what is observable here: the main
carriageway is divided by a kerbed median, so a U-turn across it is
prohibited by the road itself. There is no No-U-turn sign in view, so
sign evidence is NOT claimed. The manoeuvre must also end up against
the flow of the lane it started in.
The gate is a TRANSITION from motion to rest, not a threshold, and both
halves are load-bearing. Measured over 659210 real track pairs on
data_video2, box IoU reaches 0.97 in ordinary queued traffic, because
the camera looks obliquely down the carriageway and the lead vehicle's
box covers the one behind it (scripts/measure_interaction_metrics.py).
So:
1. Contact is judged in the ROAD frame, not the image. A queue is
separated ALONG the road by about a car length; a collision is
separated in neither direction. contact_along_px 45 and
contact_across_px 70.
2. The pair must be AT REST now and MUST have been MOVING over the
preceding approach_window. 'At rest' alone admits every pair in a
standing queue. 'Was moving' alone admits a fast pass-through, where
the tracker carries the boxes through each other so overlap and
heading change both look like contact while neither vehicle stops.
3. Only one of the pair needs to have been moving: in a rear-end
collision only the striking vehicle stops abruptly.
This took accident from 28 segments to 7 on data_video2, on a video with
no visible collision. The 7 that remain are candidates, not confirmed
events. Two vehicles are required; a pedestrian conflict belongs to
failure_to_yield, which judges the crossing geometry.
Defined by the evasive action itself: a finite TTC inside a small gap
AND a sharp deceleration or heading change. Braking to a queue at a
signal has no closing partner, so it cannot produce this event, which
is what separates it from ordinary queue behaviour.
Depends on the detector exposing obstacle-like categories. The
competition checkpoint is trained on the eight road-user classes and
emits nothing that maps to an obstacle, so with it this rule stays
silent rather than guessing. Discrimination when such classes exist:
persistence on the carriageway, and not moving away.
Same dependency as road_obstacle: needs a detector class for fire or
smoke. The competition checkpoint has none, so the rule cannot fire
with it. Documented rather than approximated with a colour heuristic,
which would fire on brake lights and sunlight.

note: The pre-collision ramp is built on min_conflict_ttc, the minimum TTC over
pairs that share a calibrated lane (or involve a pedestrian) and are actually
closing. A raw minimum over all pairs is a measure of traffic density: 30
vehicles in a queue always contain a pair with a short TTC. Measured on
data_video2, using the raw minimum put 177 of 180 frames above the official
0.5 alarm threshold, i.e. a constant alarm. See scripts/validate_risk_causality.py.
_note: Every pixel threshold in this block is expressed in the 3840x2160
reference resolution and scaled to the actual frame by
src/risk/features.py (REFERENCE_WIDTH). The same camera delivers this
intersection at 3840x2160 and 1920x1080, so a fixed pixel distance is
twice as permissive at 4K for the same physical separation. That was a
real bug: measured on data_video1 at 4K the score saturated, with 97.5%
of frames above the official 0.5 alarm threshold and a single 307s
alarm run, while the same code on data_video2 at 1080p produced 0%.
The values below are the data_video2 measurements (at 1080p) doubled, so
the scale reproduces exactly what was measured: near_distance_px 180,
pedestrian_distance_px 140.
The pre-collision ramp is built on min_conflict_ttc, the minimum TTC over
pairs that share a calibrated lane (or involve a pedestrian), are
genuinely closing, and are closer than a car length in the road frame.
A raw minimum over all pairs is a measure of traffic density: thirty
vehicles in a queue always contain a pair with a short TTC. Measured on
data_video2, using the raw minimum put 177 of 180 frames above the
official 0.5 alarm threshold, i.e. a constant alarm. See
scripts/validate_risk_causality.py and scripts/measure_risk_terms.py.
_scoring_constants: ttc_floor 0.35: the value a confirmed imminent conflict starts from.
Deliberately below the official 0.5 alarm threshold, so the other
interaction terms decide when an alarm is actually raised.
ttc_ramp_sec 2.0: the ramp is SHORTER than the 5 s reporting horizon
on purpose. The score is a confidence that a collision is imminent,
not a countdown, and a pair still 4 s away is not yet risk. Measured
effect on data_video1 (4K, busiest sample): frames at or above the
alarm threshold fell 97.5% -> 80% -> 16% as the conflict gate, the
evasive threshold and this ramp length were added, each after the
previous measure showed which term was saturating.
_high_end_not_calibrated: There is no confirmed accident in either sample video, so there is no
positive example to calibrate the HIGH end of this score against. Every
threshold here was chosen to keep ordinary traffic LOW and the score
in range, which is what a chance-normalised AP rewards; the magnitude
of the score near a real collision is unvalidated. This is stated rather
than hidden, and it is the main outstanding Part B limitation.
